structuredSummary.purpose: This procedure aims to ensure the safe and uninterrupted operation of the LNG Regasification Unit (ORU) by establishing standardized maintenance practices for process equipment, piping systems, instrumentation, and safety systems. It further establishes a comprehensive, structured, and standardized maintenance guideline for CIMC T75 LNG ISO Tanks (Chapter 8), and a standardized maintenance and inspection program to sustain plant integrity across the Nias Gasification LNG facility (Chapter 9).
keyRequirements: Yearly Maintenance Plan and Monthly Maintenance Plan must be prepared and must include periodical inspection items of the ORU System and ISO Tank, PMS items, and other important repair items.

Critical equipment and systems (LNG ISO Tank, AAV, NG Buffer Tank, NG Metering Skid, PSV, ESD, Fire & Gas Detection) are treated as top priority and require a 'Permit of Critical Equipment Maintenance' plus a 'Risk Assessment Sheet' approved by Nias Site before maintenance.

PMS (Planned Maintenance System) must cover Condition-Based/Predictive Maintenance, Risk-Based Inspection, time/run-hour based Preventive Maintenance, Regulatory Compliance calibration, parts replacement, and specialist maintenance.
All measuring equipment and tools must be calibrated through an organization-approved calibration laboratory, requested via Repair Requisition Sheet within 3 months before the due date.

ISO Tank maintenance requires Daily, Weekly, Monthly, and Annual periodic inspections, 2-year PSV/safety device replacement, and 5-year full internal inspection with classification society recertification.
Tank must be fully emptied, drained, and purged with nitrogen until oxygen concentration is <= 3% before any ISO Tank maintenance work.
Insulation vacuum integrity must be maintained at <= 0.1 Pa; degraded vacuum requires arranging re-vacuuming and a helium leak test.
Replacement PSVs must be set to 0.79-0.83 MPa and nitrogen leak-tested at 0.2-0.3 MPa before returning to service.

Subcontractor maintenance requires a Repair Requisition, Site Manager approval after Sr. Operation Team Leader review, a Work Permit for dangerous work, and review of the Work Completion Report before closing.

Maintenance and inspection execution must follow Work Preparation, Worksite Preparation (PTW, LOTO, depressurization, gas-freeing), Task Execution per OEM/API/ASME/NFPA standards with NDT, Quality & Safety Verification, and System Restoration/Handover with Work Order closure in CMMS.
Major spare parts must be identified, stocked, and jointly controlled in the computerized PMS program, with immediate resupply requests when stock is insufficient.
Maintenance records (PMS program, Log Book, Measuring reports, Monthly Maintenance Report) must be kept and reported to the Organization/Nias Site at defined intervals.
Logbook and supporting ISO Tank maintenance/inspection records must be retained for a minimum of 10 years.
Gas sales metering maintenance and meter calibration must follow AGA/ISO 5167/OIML standards to ensure custody-transfer measurement accuracy.

safetyRules: Tank must be purged with nitrogen until oxygen concentration is <= 3% before any ISO Tank maintenance work (Sec 8.6, 8.11).
Insulation vacuum must remain <= 0.1 Pa under ambient/warm conditions; if exceeded, re-vacuuming and helium leak test must be arranged (Sec 8.7, 8.11).
Replacement Pressure Safety Valve set pressure rating must be 0.79-0.83 MPa (Sec 8.11).
Nitrogen leak test after PSV replacement must be performed at 0.2-0.3 MPa (Sec 8.11).
LNG holding time must remain >= 71 days at 90% filling ratio; daily evaporation rate must remain within spec (<=0.22%/d for LN2) (Sec 8.7, NP05-09).
Hot work is strictly prohibited on ISO Tanks unless certified gas-free by HSE personnel with a Permit to Work (Sec 8.6).
Full PPE is mandatory: cryogenic gloves, face shield, anti-static coverall, safety helmet, safety shoes (Sec 8.6).
Tools used for ISO Tank work must be cryogenic service rated, anti-static, non-sparking, and calibrated (Sec 8.6).
Abnormal conditions (vacuum loss, leak, frost, structural damage) must be reported immediately and the tank withdrawn from service (Sec 8.6).
Gas test must confirm < 10% LEL before gas sales meter calibration hot/cold work begins (App 04.6).
Grounding/earthing continuity must be <= 5 Ohm (NP05-20, NP05-21).
Sorbent activation temperature must remain < 120C using dry nitrogen or oil-free hot air with dew point < -40C (NP05-09).
Work Permit (Hot/Cold), Gas Test Result, PPE Inspection, and Environmental Check verification are mandatory prerequisites before executing any periodic maintenance form (NP05-11 through NP05-37).

items.description: Valve Disassembly: Follow proper sequence, avoid damage
Cleaning: Clean metal parts with industrial cleaner, rubber with hot water
Drying: Blow dry with clean, low-pressure nitrogen
Seal Replacement: Replace worn or deformed seals per spec
Reinstallation: Ensure clean joint surfaces and correct positioning
Documentation: Attach retest report and certificate for replaced valves
Pressure Gauge (P): Verify range, accuracy, and responsiveness
Liquid Level Gauge (L): Confirm zero calibration, responsiveness, and no blockage
Gas Phase Gauge Valve (G-1): Check for leakage and proper open/close function
Liquid Phase Gauge Valve (G-3): Inspect for tightness and valve sensitivity
Equalization Valve (G-2): Confirm proper operation during gauge calibration
Thermocouple Tube (VM-1): Inspect for damage and verify vacuum reading capability
Composite Transmitter (SMTR-2-LTP-GB): Check liquid level, pressure, and temperature readings; verify explosion-proof certification
Wiring & Connectors: Inspect for corrosion, loose terminals, or insulation damage
Display Panel / Indicators: Confirm visibility, accuracy, and alarm function (if applicable)
Calibration Records: Verify latest calibration date and documentation
Sensor Mounting: Ensure secure installation and no vibration-induced loosening
Moisture Check in Gauge Lines: Inspect for condensation or ice blockage in narrow tubing
Tank Pressure Reduction: Reduce tank pressure to <= 0.1 MPa
Cryogenic Liquid Discharge: Fully discharge LNG from inner vessel
Nitrogen Purge: Purge tank with dry nitrogen to remove moisture
Ambient Temperature Recovery: Allow inner vessel to warm gradually
PPE Check: Confirm use of gloves, goggles, anti-static gear

checklists.title: Checklist - Vacuum & Insulation Integrity ISO Tank

items.description: Evidence of frost or condensation on outer shell: Visual inspection for frozen grain, moisture, or frost patches
Sudden pressure rise in inner vessel: Monitor pressure gauge (P); abnormal rise may indicate vacuum loss
Daily evaporation rate: Compare with spec; perform evaporation test if needed
Thermocouple tube (VM-1) reading: Check vacuum level via thermocouple tube; verify against baseline
Outer shell pressure relief device (B-1): Inspect for proper sealing and activation readiness
Insulation layer integrity: Confirm no signs of insulation collapse or displacement
Sorbent activation status: Verify last activation date and condition of molecular sorbent
Heated pipe sealing: Ensure sorbent heating pipes are properly plugged to prevent moisture ingress
Vacuum interlayer rupture disc: Check for signs of rupture or corrosion; replace if damaged
Vacuum loss indicators: Any combination of frost, pressure rise, or sorbent failure
Activation temperature control: Confirm activation temperature < 120C during last treatment
Activation gas purity: Ensure dry nitrogen or oil-free hot air was used (dew point < -40C)

structuredSummary.purpose: NP-06 establishes the process for managing contractors, vendors, and subcontractors who provide materials or services to PT. LNG Nias Gasification, including the Contractor Safety Management System (CSMS) for risk-based HSE qualification and monitoring of third parties. It also governs requisition, purchasing, receiving/tallying, inventory control, and the full vendor/subcontractor management lifecycle (selection, contracting, KPI-based performance evaluation, and corrective action) to ensure third-party work complies with PT. LNG quality, cost, schedule, and HSE standards.
keyRequirements: Contractor work is classified into three CSMS risk categories (Category 1 High, Category 2 Medium, Category 3 Low) based on potential impact to process safety, personnel, and the environment.

All contractors must be pre-qualified before entering the bidder list; medium/high-risk contractors must submit a complete CSMS document unless exempted, and low-risk contractors require HSE Policy review only.
CSMS Pre-Qualification certificates are valid for 2 years and may be reviewed or cancelled on organizational change, regulatory violation, or unsatisfactory performance.

Vendor/contractor selection is evaluated on Legality (20%), Experience (20%), Finance (20%), HR & Competence (15%), HSE Performance (15%), and Infrastructure (10%), with a minimum passing score of 75/100.
An HSE Plan is mandatory for contracts exceeding 1 year with at least 10 POB, or high-risk projects under 1 year with more than 50 POB, and must be approved by the QHSE Manager and Contract Owner.
Contract lifecycle follows Drafting -> Negotiation -> Signing -> Implementation -> Monitoring & Control -> Amendment -> Closure, with mandatory SOW, HSE Clause, and penalty terms.

Vendor/subcontractor performance is monitored daily, monthly, quarterly, and annually, and scored using a weighted KPI formula: Quality 30%, Delivery 25%, Cost Control 15%, HSE 20%, Support & Communication 10%.
Evaluation results classify vendors as Excellent (>=85%), Good (70-84%), Fair (50-69%), or Poor (<50%, blacklisted and removed from the Approved Vendor List).
Subcontractor selection requires identification of necessity, collection/analysis of subcontractor status, and approval by the Site Manager and top management representative.
Subcontractor registration is cancelled for critical product/service defects, a periodical assessment score below 60 points, or management decision.
Store/spare-part requisitions (NP06-07/NP06-08) must be submitted 7 days ahead of the estimated supply date (1 month for periodic stores supply).
Inventory List (NP06-09) must be updated immediately upon any stock change and submitted in May and November; Important Spare Part List is submitted quarterly.
Received goods must be tallied against invoice/requisition specifications, with non-conforming or missing items recorded on the Receiving/Tally Report (NP06-17).

Nonconformities are classified as Major, Minor, or Observation, and processed through Identification -> NCR -> Root Cause Analysis -> Corrective Action Plan -> Implementation -> Verification -> Closure.
Document retention periods are defined: Contracts & SPK 10 years, HSE Reports 5 years, Daily Reports 2 years, Permit to Work 1 year.
approvalLine: Approved by: Daniel Kweon (System Management Leader)
safetyRules: Medium- and high-risk contractors must complete CSMS Pre-Qualification, including HSE Questionnaire review and hazard management documentation, before bidding.

Mandatory Safety Induction topics include HSE Policy, Emergency Procedures, PPE, PTW System, Incident Reporting, Isolation Energy (LOTO), Working at Height (WAH) & Confined Space Entry (CSE), and Process Safety Fundamentals.
Hot Work requires helmet, heat-resistant gloves, welding glasses, and an available fire extinguisher (APAR), authorized by Supervisor + HSE.
Working at Height (fall risk above 1.8m) requires full body harness, helmet, and lifeline, authorized by Supervisor + HSE.
Confined Space Entry requires a gas detector, SCBA, and a standby man, authorized by Supervisor + HSE.
HSE Compliance SLA target is 100% Zero Accident; any Lost Time Injury (LTI) results in vendor blacklisting.

Controlled drugs (Codeine Sulphate, Diazepam, Morphine Sulphate, Phenobarbital) must be kept locked in the Site Manager's secure accommodation, issued only by the Site Manager, with all issuance recorded in the Medical Logbook.

The Contractor Job Inspection HSE Checklist (NP06-22) must verify housekeeping, PPE, fire prevention, hazard communication, electrical safety, confined space entry, scaffolding, and excavation controls before and during work execution.
The Company reserves the right to terminate contractor work immediately for serious HSE violations under the mandatory HSE Clause.

structuredSummary.purpose: This document establishes the standard operating procedures for LNG cargo handling operations at the Nias Onshore LNG Regasification Terminal, covering ISO tank yard management, lifting and transport, unloading skid operation, ambient air vaporizer (AAV) operation, gas sales metering, and ship-to-ship (STS) ISO tank transfer. It defines safe, efficient, and compliant methods for receiving, storing, unloading, regasifying, and metering LNG from ISO tank containers for pipeline distribution to the offtaker.
keyRequirements: ISO tanks must be inspected on arrival (general, pre-use, monthly/annual) and separated into FULL/EMPTY yard zones per Tank Condition Report.

Yard storage must maintain minimum safe distances (3 m between full tanks, 5 m to non-hazardous tanks, 7.5 m from boundaries, 15 m from buildings/critical infrastructure) with a maximum 2-tier stacking rule, full tanks bottom tier only.

Lifting operations require certified equipment (crane certified by ESDM Migas/KEMENAKER/BKI, spreader beam SWL >= total load), a 20-30 cm pre-lift test, and total lifted load capped at 85% of crane SWL.
FIFO must be applied for full ISO tank switching, subject to Go/No-Go criteria on documentation, physical condition, pressure/temperature, and product level.
Unloading skid operation follows a defined pre-cooling, switching threshold (scale weight/level gauge), and safe depressurization sequence, with grounding cable removed last during disconnection.
Shift handover occurs every 12 hours with joint walkthrough, parameter logging, and dual signature on the Change Shift Checklist (Form NP08-08).
AAV units operate in a 4-duty/2-standby configuration, switched to standby when fin frost exceeds 70% of surface area, monitored every 30 minutes.
Gas sales metering uses a dual-train (Run A duty / Run B standby) configuration with a defined line-switching and calibration sequence requiring PTW, LOTO, and gas testing before work.
Flexible hoses and QCC couplers require daily visual inspection, periodic nitrogen static leak testing (1.1x MAWP) and pressure testing (1.5x working pressure) with zero leak acceptance criteria.

Ship-to-ship (STS) ISO tank transfer requires a valid Syahbandar STS Operation Permit and compliance with weather limits (wind < 20 knots, wave < 1.0 m, visibility > 1 nautical mile, current < 1.5 knots).
Delegation of Authority (DOA) must be formally documented via Form NP08-38 whenever the Site Manager or Sr. O&M Leader is off-duty.
Atmospheric gas monitoring must be logged at defined intervals at each unloading skid, verifying O2 19.5-23.5% and LEL below 10%.
Field Operators hold Stop Work Authority (SWA) and must log parameters hourly (ISO tank) and every 4 hours (plant).
Emergency response for LNG leaks/spills is scaled by severity (minor: isolate and cover with wet cloth/dry sand; major: trigger ESD, evacuate 50-100 m radius).
Yard inventory must be tracked in real time (tank number, status, position, pressure/level, condition) with daily walkdown and weekly reconciliation.
approvalLine: Juli Surungan Aprianto Simanjuntak - Operation Team Leader (Prepared by)
Shadiq Muhammad - Sr. Operation Leader (Prepared by)
Daniel Kweon - System Management Leader (Approved by)
safetyRules: Multi-point gas testing required before unloading: LEL < 10%, O2 19.5%-23.5%.
Grounding clamp must be attached and tested to a resistance target of < 5 Ohm; grounding cable must be removed LAST after hose disconnection.
Never enter an area with O2 < 19.5% without Self-Contained Breathing Apparatus (SCBA).
Minor LNG leak: isolate and restrict area to 25 m radius, cover leak with wet cloth (never spray water on liquid LNG).
Major LNG leak/rupture: trigger ESD, evacuate personnel to 50-100 m radius, declare supply interruption if switching is impossible.
LNG spill on ground: cover with dry sand for natural evaporation, close drains; do NOT spray water directly on liquid LNG.
ISO tank must be depressurized to Vent Stack (VT-101) until reaching 0.4 MPa, or below 0.05 MPa before hose disconnection.
Sling angle between wire rope and spreader beam must not exceed a minimum of 45 degrees; no walking under suspended loads; tag lines mandatory.
STS transfer requires methane LEL = 0% confirmed by gas test and compliance with weather limits (wind < 20 knots, wave < 1.0 m).
AAV units must be checked for structural cracks/deformation after thawing; venting must be directed to Vent Stack (VT-101) or flare (methane GWP ~25x CO2).
Metering line switching/calibration requires approved PTW, JSA, LOTO, and gas test (<10% LEL) before work.
PBU system PRV setpoint fixed at 0.75 MPa (11.7 barg); pipeline send-out pressure design/safety limit is max 85 barg.

title: NIAS NP-09 Procedure for Risk Assessment and Safety Management

structuredSummary.purpose: The purpose of this procedure is to provide a systematic approach to risk assessment, ensuring that risks associated with tasks are reduced to an acceptable level, personnel are competent in evaluating risks, assessments are reviewed periodically or when changes occur, and compliance with applicable legislative requirements is maintained. It further establishes a systematic process for identifying, assessing, controlling, and monitoring health, safety, environmental, and operational risks associated with all activities at the mini-LNG regasification facility, with the goal of eliminating or reducing risks to a level that is As Low As Reasonably Practicable (ALARP).
keyRequirements: Use the Preliminary Risk Assessment Checklist (PRAC) to identify hazards before work begins (Stage 1), answering Yes/No in Column 1, mitigation in Column 2, and ALARP confirmation in Column 3.

For a job-specific risk assessment with a clear job step, a Job Safety Analysis (JSA) methodology and JSA Form shall be conducted at minimum; non-job-specific assessments may use Hazid methodology (inductive or deductive).
The Risk Assessment team must comprise a minimum of two persons, including a Risk Assessment-trained Team Leader with correct skills, information and knowledge.
PRAC/Risk Assessment must be integrated with the Permit to Work (PTW) system; Work Permit applications must attach the completed PRAC, Risk Assessment, and supporting documentation.

A Pre-Job Safety Meeting (PJSM) is required for all tasks, formal or informal, to brief the work team on hazards and risk reduction measures, with names/signatures/dates recorded to confirm understanding.
PRAC/Risk Assessment must be revalidated whenever there is a break in work continuity of more than 24 hours, a change of Work Leader/Responsible Person, or a significant change to the method of work.
Routine non-Work Permit tasks must follow the same PRAC/Risk Assessment steps as Work Permit tasks and be reviewed every 12 months or upon task change.

Hazard identification methods include Process Hazard Analysis (PHA/HAZOP), Job Safety Analysis (JSA), Management of Change (MOC), Workplace Inspections & Audits, Incident & Near-Miss Investigation, and open Hazard Reporting.
Risk is calculated as Risk Score = Severity x Likelihood, each rated 1-5, using the 5x5 Risk Matrix Table.
Risk Acceptance Criteria classify scores into EXTREME (15-25), HIGH (8-12), MEDIUM (4-6), and LOW (1-3) bands with corresponding mandatory actions.
Risk control follows the Hierarchy of Controls in order: Elimination, Substitution, Engineering Controls, Administrative Controls, and Personal Protective Equipment (PPE).

New risks/near-misses must be reported to the Safety & Environmental Officer, recorded by the SSHQE Officer via Form Incident Accident Investigation Report (NP11-01), and reviewed for addition to the Risk Register by the SYSMAN Team Leader.
The entire Risk Register must be formally reviewed annually by HSE & Operations Manager; specific risk assessments must be redone after major incidents or Management of Change (MOC).

Specialized task types (hazardous chemicals, manual handling, PPE, noise, computer workstations, work equipment, lead exposure, confined space entry, lifting operations) require supplementary or specific risk/task assessments as detailed in Section 7.
PRAC records must be kept for at least 1 year and archived with the Work Permit for a further 5 years; Risk Assessments must be stored electronically in discreet asset/function folders.

safetyRules: AAV Purging & Inerting: N2 purging until hydrocarbons <1% LEL and O2 <2%, with AGT verification.
AAV Maintenance Removal of Inert Atmosphere: Positive pressure N2 purge with O2 <2% verification before controlled cooldown.
AAV Operation Low Outlet Temperature Trip: Low-temp trip setpoint -5°C, with downstream Knock-Out Drum and auto-switchover.
AAV Pre-Commissioning Pressure Test: N2 test at 1.5x MAWP with remote pressurization and exclusion zone.
Cryogenic Hose Isolation & Decommissioning: Gas test <10% LEL required after double block valve LOTO and N2 purge.
Cryogenic Hose Proof/Pressure Testing: 1.5x MAWP test conducted within a test enclosure/barrier cell with remote operation.
ESD During Unloading: Immediate activation triggers include manual E-Stop, high gas detection (>60% LEL), fire detection, or low line pressure.
Gas Sales Metering Maintenance Inert Removal & Gas Purging: Natural gas purge to vent stack until O2 <0.5%, verified with a portable O2 analyzer.
LNG ISO Tank Ship Berthing: Docking Aid System approach speed must be <5 cm/s during vessel maneuvering.
LNG ISO Tank Ship Berthing Safety Zone: 50-meter extended hazardous zone with continuous methane detection along the quay.
LNG ISO Tank Yard Management: Minimum 15m spacing between tanks under one-way traffic layout.
LNG ISO Tank Yard Management: Impoundment basin sized to 110% of largest tank capacity.
LNG ISO Tank Yard Management BOG Pressure Monitoring: SCADA real-time monitoring with High-High alarms and operator rounds every 2-4 hours.
Cryogenic Gloves must be loose-fitting and designed to protect against temperatures down to -162°C; they are NOT liquid-proof.
Hearing Protection is required in areas where 8-hour TWA exceeds 85 dBA or 12-hour TWA exceeds 83 dBA.
A Noise Assessment is required when noise levels of 85dB(A) for 8 hours exposure or 83dB(A) for 12 hours exposure occurs.
Risk Acceptance: EXTREME (15 - 25) is UNACCEPTABLE — operations MUST NOT commence or must cease until adequate controls are implemented.
Risk Acceptance: HIGH (8 - 12) is UNDESIRABLE — requires temporary controls until permanent solutions are in place.
Risk Acceptance: MEDIUM (4 - 6) is TOLERABLE — must be managed by specific procedures and controls with assigned monitoring responsibility.
Risk Acceptance: LOW (1 - 3) is ACCEPTABLE — managed by routine procedures with ongoing monitoring.
PRAC/Risk Assessment must be revalidated if there has been a break in continuity of the work for more than 24 hours.
The Risk Assessment team must comprise a minimum of two persons, including a Risk Assessment-trained Team Leader.
Non-Routine/High Risk Tasks (Hot Work, Confined Space Entry, Line Breaking, Emergency Response) require: gas testing before/during work, a standby person assigned, and an emergency plan in place.
Electrical System (MCC, Panels) work requires strict LOTO compliance plus a work permit and electrical work permit.
PRAC records must be kept for at least 1 year and archived with the work permit for a further 5 years.

Severity Rating Scale (Consequence) — assess Personnel Safety & Health, Environmental Impact, Asset/Financial Impact, and Reputation Impact to select a Severity score of 1-5.
options: 1 - Negligible: No injury or minor first aid; No impact or negligible spill; Negligible repair cost; No impact.
2 - Minor: Medical Treatment Case (MTC) or First Aid; Minor spill contained on-site, minor cleanup; < $10,000; Minor equipment damage; Internal investigation, no external attention.

3 - Moderate: Lost Time Injury (LTI); Localized containment failure, reportable release to authorities; $10,000 - $100,000; Significant repair needed; Local media attention, complaints from local community.

4 - Major: Severe injury, permanent partial disability; Significant release requiring external cleanup and major regulatory reporting; $100,000 - $1,000,000; Major equipment loss; Regional media attention, significant regulatory fines.

5 - Catastrophic: Fatality or permanent total disability; Major release with severe, long-term environmental damage, Regulatory shutdown; > $1,000,000; Total loss of facility; National media attention, major legal charges, loss of license to operate.

items.description: Likelihood Rating Scale (Probability) — select a Likelihood score of 1-5 based on frequency definition.
options: 1 - Rare: May occur only in exceptional circumstances; Less than once in 30 years; Example: Vapor Cloud Explosion (VCE) with blast effects.
2 - Unlikely: Could happen but rare; Once in 10-30 years; Example: Major leak from a primary process line.
3 - Possible: Might occur at some time; Once every 3-10 years; Example: Overpressure event contained by a safety valve.
4 - Likely: Will probably occur; Once every 1-3 years; Example: Failure of a pump seal causing a localized leak.
5 - Almost Certain: Expected to occur; Once per year or more; Example: Minor LNG spill during routine truck unloading.

items.passFailCriteria: EXTREME (15 - 25): UNACCEPTABLE. Immediate action required to mitigate risk. Operations MUST NOT commence or must cease until adequate controls are implemented. Requires senior management intervention and a detailed risk reduction plan.

HIGH (8 - 12): UNDESIRABLE. Senior management attention needed. Specific mitigation plans with defined responsibilities and timelines must be established. Requires temporary controls until permanent solutions are in place.

MEDIUM (4 - 6): TOLERABLE. Must be managed by specific procedures and controls. Responsibility for monitoring must be assigned. Efforts to reduce risk further should be evaluated based on cost/benefit (ALARP principle).
LOW (1 - 3): ACCEPTABLE. Managed by routine procedures. No additional controls are typically required, but monitoring is necessary to ensure the risk level does not increase.

structuredSummary.purpose: It is a requirement of PT. LNG's SSHQE Management System Element 8 that incidents will be reported, investigated, analysed and communicated to prevent recurrence and improve SSHQE performance, with Root Cause Analysis (RCA) used to identify root causes and system failures. The purpose of this procedure is to assure incidents are reported so response actions are effectively provided, steps are taken to prevent recurrence of similar incidents, and legal requirements are met, by standardizing incident classification, reporting, investigation, and lessons-learned sharing.

Incident Command System with defined roles: Incident Commander (Site Manager), Incident Coordinator, HSE/Safety Officer, Public Information Officer, Liaison Officer, Operations/Logistics/Finance Section Chiefs (App 03.1.2, App 04.2).
Three-tier incident command structure for ISO Tank operations: Level 1 (First Intervention Team local response), Level 2 (Facility ERT), Level 3 (External/Corporate escalation) (App 10.5, App 14.4).
Standardized notification chain: Discoverer -> Control Room -> O&M Team Leader -> Site Manager -> External Services (App 04.5).

Major Incident Notification (Level 5-4): immediate report to emergency line/Team Leader, escalation to Site Manager/HSE Officer, and PT. LNG Major Incident Announcement Form submitted to Board of Directors within 8 hours (2.5.1).
DAFWC/Level 3 Notification: Initial Incident Announcement Form completed and emailed to Operation Director, Site Manager, and Senior Managers within 24 hours (2.5.2).
Government (MIGAS) reporting: fatalities/DAFWC > 21 days reported via Form IIIi/IIIp within 24 hours; hydrocarbon/chemical spills > 15 bbls reported via Form LPL-1 within 48 hours (2.5.4).
Root Cause Analysis (RCA) methodology mandatory for all investigations, with report deadlines: Level 5-4 per approved Terms of Reference, Level 3 within 7 days, Level 2-1 within 3 days (2.6).

Incident classification per US OSHA 29 CFR 1904 and Incident Risk Assessment Matrix (IRAM) Level 1-5 severity across Health & Safety, Environmental, Asset/Business, Security, and LOPC categories (2.9).
Lesson Learned Flyer (1-page, bilingual Bahasa Indonesia/English) required within 3 days after investigation report completion for Major Incidents, distributed to site notice boards (2.8).
Mandatory competency and training for all personnel involved in incident reporting/RCA; role-specific ICS, HAZWOPER, and cryogenic safety training required (2.7, App 03.2).
Scheduled emergency drills: Major LNG Leak & Vapor Cloud (6-monthly), Class C Fire (3-monthly), Medical Emergency (3-monthly), Earthquake/Tsunami (3-monthly), Integrated Drill (Annual) (App 04.10).
Emergency Operations Plan (EOP) covers hazard-specific procedures for tsunami, earthquake, fire, LNG leakage, and dangerous reptile encounters, ISO 45001 Clause 8.2 compliant (App 03.1).
Emergency Shutdown (ESD) activation levels (Level 1 Unit ESD, Level 2 Process ESD, Level 3 Full Facility ESD) with defined ESD sequence and 7-step ESD action procedure (App 04.4).
Media control restricts official accident-related communications to a designated spokesperson/PRESS Company third party under Site Manager approval (1.4).

safetyRules: Danger Zone: Minimum 50m radius from leak per NFPA 59A (App 10.2, App 14.2).
LNG Leak scenario: Establish 50m hot zone; roadblocks 500m downwind for offsite areas (App 02.2 Scenario 1).
LNG Pool Fire: Evacuate 1km radius, close highways downwind (App 02.2 Scenario 2).
Vapor Cloud Fire: Community sirens, reverse 911 to 5km zone (App 02.2 Scenario 3).
Rapid Phase Transition (RPT): Retreat >=500m, avoid water application to LNG (App 02.2 Scenario 4).
Man Overboard: Deploy rescue boat within 3 mins (App 02.2 Scenario 11).
Fire on Vessel: 3km maritime exclusion zone, airspace restriction (App 02.2 Scenario 9).
Cryogenic Equipment Failure: Monitor O2 deficiency (<19.5%) (App 02.2 Scenario 20).
Flammable gas detection (infrared/ultrasonic) set at <25% LFL; automated alarm for LNG Leakage activates at >25% LFL (App 03.1.4).
Class 2 Site Emergency alarm: Continuous alarm for 3 minutes (App 04.1, App 04.1.2).
Class 3 General Emergency alarm: Intermittent alarm on/off cycles (App 04.1, App 04.1.2).
All Clear signal: Single long tone (1 minute) (App 04.1.2).
Standby power backup minimum 30 mins for emergency communication technical systems (App 04.5).
Grounding clamp resistance must be <= 5 Ω before operation (App 10.6; NP11-12 item 4).
Pre-lift exclusion zone >= 10m; test lift raises load 0.5-1m for stability check (App 10.6).
ISO Tank walk-around pressure check range: 3-7 bar (App 10.6).
Alarm tones (App 10.7): Continuous 10s tone = vapor/leak; Intermittent bursts = fire; Prolonged 30s tone = full evacuation.
ISO Tank Popping: Evacuate 50m radius; re-entry only when pressure stabilizes < 0.70 MPa and gas is clear (App 10.8).

High Pressure/Overpressure thresholds (App 13.3): PSV setpoint 0.84-0.88 MPa; manageable example 0.78-0.80 MPa; equalize pressure up to ~0.75 MPa; depressurize to vent stack down to ~0.40 MPa; approaching PSV ≈0.83 MPa; PSV re-seating at ~0.70 MPa.
LNG Leakage isolation safety perimeter: 50-100m exclusion zone; report status every 10 min; monitor gas detectors every 5 min; perimeter gas test every 15 min (App 13.3).
Minor Fire Near Hose/Connection: monitor 30-60 min for re-ignition (App 13.3).
Major Fire at ISO Tank Body/Manifold: 100m exclusion zone; continuous cooling for min 60 mins post-extinguishing (App 13.3).
Ignition Without Visible Fire (Flash Fireball): evacuate downwind min 200m; continuous gas test (<10% LEL safe) (App 13.3).
Fire Escalation Threatening Multiple Tanks: total evacuation 300m radius; post-fire water cooling for min 2 hours (App 13.3).
Post-Fire Recovery: water cooling 60-120 min post-fire (App 13.3).
ESD Failure or Valve Stuck Open: Evacuate 100m radius (App 13.3).
Abnormal Vapor Release: if >10% LEL expand exclusion zone; apply LOTO once safe (<1% LEL) (App 13.3).
Structural Damage or Tank Rollover: establish min 100m exclusion zone (App 13.3).
Popping/Venting Event (ISO Tank Mobilization): evacuate personnel min 50m upwind (gas detector verified) (App 14.4).
Spill/Leak Event (ISO Tank Mobilization): evacuate min 50m upwind; do NOT touch -162°C liquid (App 14.4).
Personnel Injury & Medical Evacuation: evacuate to safe assembly point radius >=50m (App 14.4).
Ambient Air Vaporizer Frost Hazard: frost covering >70% AAV surface triggers standby unit switch (App 12.3).
NP11-11 Emergency Action Checklist requires Gas Test Result recorded in % LEL and PPE Inspection marked Passed before authorization.
NP11-12 Emergency Preparedness Checklist item 4: grounding continuity must be <= 5 Ω, clamp attached before operation.

Risk assessment conducted per NP-09 Procedure for Risk Assessment and Safety Management
Risk rating 1 or 2: acceptable, no additional mitigation needed
Risk rating 4 or 5: not acceptable, requires additional mitigation per NP-09
Risk rating 3: necessity of mitigation decided through further review
Team leader submits Plan of Change, Risk Assessment Sheet, and Risk Improvement Plan to Site Manager for approval
After completion, team leader draws up 'Completion of Change' report (Form NP12-02) including final risk assessment and training completed
Extension requests for temporary/permanent change require Site Manager review and approval
Site Manager reviews effectiveness of change (procedure followed, completed within time scale, risk measures taken, manuals updated) via quarterly SSHQE meeting and yearly management review
